subject.title: Telegram: unquarantine skipped sticker e2e tests

question: Should Telegram still require a dedicated static WEBP sticker metadata e2e case, or is the current lower-level/cache-refresh coverage sufficient to close this issue?
rationale: Current main only partially matches the original unskip criteria, and the live protected labels explicitly route the remaining coverage choice to maintainers rather than an autonomous fix lane.

options.title: Require the static WEBP e2e
options.body: Keep this issue open and add one deterministic e2e case that proves the `<media:sticker>` payload metadata for a first-seen static WEBP sticker.

options.title: Accept current coverage
options.body: Close this issue after a maintainer states that resolver, context, and cache-refresh tests cover the risk well enough without the original e2e title.

recommendation.title: Require the static WEBP e2e
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and add one deterministic e2e case that proves the `<media:sticker>` payload metadata for a first-seen static WEBP sticker.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the stabilization PR that quarantined the tests and created this follow-up boundary.
